faqs.q: What are the benefits of Galaxy eSIM?
faqs.a: An eSIM is an embedded SIM card that does not require a physical SIM card. An eSIM allows you to activate your device without a pSIM or physical SIM card. All you need is a mobile account and access to the network with your device. Placing domestic service on an eSIM can free up a pSIM slot for international travel. You can also use it to easily activate an international eSIM. Dual SIM allows you to maintain two lines on a single device (one of which would be operating on the eSIM).
faqs.t: Dual SIM Phones | How to Configure pSIM and eSIM Devices | Samsung US

faqs.q: What are the benefits of Galaxy pSIM?
faqs.a: A pSIM is a physical SIM card that sits in the user's device. A pSIM allows you to quickly switch devices by swapping SIM cards in the event that your phone is damaged. In addition, it allows for a local prepaid pSIM to be used internationally as a more cost-effective option than adding an international package to your phone’s main line. Dual SIM allows you to maintain two lines on a single device (one of which would be operating on the pSIM).
faqs.t: Dual SIM Phones | How to Configure pSIM and eSIM Devices | Samsung US

faqs.q: What does 4K resolution mean on a TV?
faqs.a: 4K resolution is a high-definition display standard that offers incredibly sharp and detailed images. It gets its name from the approximately 4,000 horizontal pixels it has (3,840 pixels across and 2,160 pixels down, denoted as "3840x2160"). A 4K TV supports this resolution, making it perfect for watching movies, shows, and playing games with stunning clarity. With four times the pixels of a standard Full HD TV (1920x1080), 4K TVs deliver crisper details, smoother visuals, and a more immersive viewing experience.
faqs.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features | Samsung USA

faqs.q: What is the difference between 4K TV and UHD TV?
faqs.a: 4K TV and UHD TV are the same, both offer 3840x2160 resolution.UHD stands for Ultra High Definition and is the consumer standard for televisions with a 3840 x 2160 pixel resolution.
faqs.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features | Samsung USA

faqs.q: Is it worth buying an 4K TV?
faqs.a: If you want the best picture quality , a 4K TV is a great choice. It's especially worth it if you're upgrading from an HD or Full HD TV. Here's why, 4K has 4x more pixels than Full HD (FHD), making images much sharper. 4K has 9x more pixels than HD, offering an even more detailed and lifelike picture. For a better viewing experience, a 4K TV is definitely worth considering.
faqs.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features | Samsung USA

faqs.q: What 4K content is available?
faqs.a: 4K content is readily accessible in various forms. This includes 4K broadcasts, streaming services, and user-generated content captured with 4K cameras and smartphones. You can find such content on platforms like YouTube. Additionally, major streaming providers like Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+, they all support 4K.
faqs.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features | Samsung USA

faqs.q: Is a 4K TV good for gaming?
faqs.a: A 4K resolution TV is ideal for gaming, as it provides a more immersive and ultra-fluid experience. Notably, the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC gaming, support 4K gaming, and Samsung Gaming TVs with HDMI 2.1 ensure a seamless 4K gaming experience.
faqs.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features | Samsung USA

faqs.q: What is 4K upscaling?
faqs.a: When you watch lower-quality FHD content on a 4K TV, upscaling is the technology that increases its resolution and optimizes it to fit the display panel of a 4K TV. It upgrades it for the 4K display. Upscaling automatically analyzes resolution to reduce noise, improve details and provide optimum contrast and color so that you can view the content in 4K-like quality.

For refresh rates above 120Hz, a PC connection is typically required. A higher refresh rate means less blur. Most Samsung TVs have a 60Hz refresh rate , which is standard for everyday viewing. faqs.q: 1. What Does OLED TV Mean?
faqs.a: An OLED TV is a type of display that uses self-lighting pixels to create its image. Unlike traditional TVs that rely on a backlight, OLED panels use organic compounds that emit light when electricity is applied — hence the name OLED, which stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. Each pixel in an OLED screen can be turned on and off, or have its brightness independently adjusted. This allows for incredibly precise control over contrast and color, resulting in deep, true blacks, vibrant visuals and ultra-responsive performance. Whether you're watching movies, gaming or streaming your favorite shows, OLED technology delivers a viewing experience that's hard to match.

faqs.q: What Does OLED TV Mean?

Unlike traditional TVs that rely on a backlight, OLED panels use organic compounds that emit light when electricity is applied — hence the name OLED, which stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. Each pixel in an OLED screen can be turned on and off, or have its brightness independently adjusted. This allows for incredibly precise control over contrast and color, resulting in deep, true blacks, vibrant visuals and ultra-responsive performance. faqs.q: What is refresh rate?
faqs.a: Refresh rate is a measure of how many times per second a display updates the image, expressed in hertz. For example, a refresh rate of 60Hz means the screen refreshes or redraws itself 60 times per second. This continuous update creates a fluid and seamless image, which is crucial when gaming. A high refresh rate provides smooth gameplay with less motion blur, keeping your game visuals clear and vivid. It also reduces input lag, so you can react quickly in intense gaming environments. Motion Xcelerator Turbo Pro on Samsung gaming TVs delivers improved clarity and smoothness during fast-moving scenes.

faqs.q: What is input lag?
faqs.a: Input lag is the time it takes for your gaming TV to recognize that you’ve pressed a button on your controller. When playing FPS (First-Person Shooter) or sports games, any delay in input can be the difference between you winning or losing the game — so it’s recommended to find a TV with a low input lag to ensure that your game is as responsive as possible. chunks.h: What is the best Samsung fridge?
chunks.x: The best Samsung fridge depends on your household needs and preferences. For example, French door models with Family Hub™ technology are great for smart home integration, while top freezer models offer classic reliability. To find the best fridge for you , consider your kitchen layout, storage needs, and whether features like smart connectivity or flexible cooling zones are a priority.

chunks.h: What are the different types of refrigerators?
chunks.x: The most common types of refrigerators include 3-door, 4-door, French door, side-by-side, top freezer, bottom freezer, and counter-depth models. Each type offers unique advantages based on space, storage habits, and design preferences. Exploring various refrigerator types can help you find the perfect fit for your kitchen and lifestyle.

chunks.t: Shop our Best Refrigerators | Stainless Steel
chunks.h: What is a smart refrigerator and how does it work?
chunks.x: A smart refrigerator connects to your home Wi-Fi and allows you to control settings, receive notifications, and monitor energy usage through a smartphone app. Features can include interior cameras, touch screens, and voice assistants. Understanding what a smart refrigerator is helps you decide if its convenience and connectivity align with your kitchen routine.

chunks.t: Shop our Best Refrigerators | Stainless Steel
chunks.h: How do I measure for a new refrigerator?
chunks.x: To measure for a refrigerator, start by measuring the height, width, and depth of the space where it will be installed. Leave extra room for ventilation and door clearance. Be sure to measure hallways and doorways for delivery as well. Knowing how to measure for a refrigerator ensures a smooth fit and avoids installation issues.

chunks.t: Shop our Best Refrigerators | Stainless Steel
chunks.h: What is the standard refrigerator size?
chunks.x: The standard refrigerator size typically ranges from 30 to 36 inches wide, 67 to 70 inches tall, and 29 to 35 inches deep. However, the ideal size depends on your kitchen layout and household needs. If you're asking what is the standard refrigerator size, be sure to factor in door swing, ventilation, and delivery path when measuring.

chunks.t: Shop our Best Refrigerators | Stainless Steel
chunks.h: What are the benefits of energy efficient refrigerators?
chunks.x: Energy efficient refrigerators use less electricity, helping you reduce utility bills and minimize environmental impact. These models often include better insulation, advanced compressors, and smart sensors to optimize performance. Choosing an energy efficient refrigerator can save money in the long run while supporting sustainable living.

chunks.t: Shop our Best Refrigerators | Stainless Steel
chunks.h: What is a garage ready refrigerator?
chunks.x: A garage ready refrigerator is designed to operate efficiently in extreme temperatures, typically ranging from 38°F to 110°F. These refrigerators have specialized compressors and insulation that allow them to maintain consistent cooling performance in unheated or non-climate-controlled spaces, such as garages or basements. If you need a second refrigerator for extra storage outside your kitchen, a garage refrigerator is a reliable and durable option. chunks.x: From the inside out, Galaxy Z TriFold has been engineered to be incredibly thin despite the expansive screen. It fits in your pocket when folded, and then unfolds to a width of 3.9 mm at its thinnest.5,6

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: Why is the design of Galaxy Z TriFold unique compared to other Galaxy devices?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold is unique because it's the first TriFold Galaxy smartphone, with an infolding form that protects the inner display. The TriFold design opens up to reveal a large display within for significantly more screen space and versatility than current foldables. The innovative dual-hinge mechanism enables a thin design that folds and unfolds smoothly. It folds into itself, helping to protect the main screen when not in use. This ensures that no part of the main screen is left exposed when fully closed.3,4

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: What size are the displays on Galaxy Z TriFold?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold has two displays: the 10" main screen and the 6.5" cover screen. The expansive 10" main screen can be used in landscape or turned vertically for an aspect ratio similar to A4 documents. The 6.5" cover screen features a wide aspect ratio, creating a comfortable typing and scrolling experience as familiar as a standard bar-type smartphone. The dual screens allow you to use it as a typical premium smartphone, then unfold to reveal a flexible display that offers more space than previous Galaxy Z models.2,3

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: How thin is Galaxy Z TriFold?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold is an impressively thin Galaxy device, thanks to its innovative design and engineering. When unfolded, it measures at 3.9 mm at its thinnest point. Folded, it's a perfectly portable 12.9 mm.5,6

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: What color does Galaxy Z TriFold come in?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold is available in Crafted Black, a unique color that amplifies the premium experience. Crafted Black features a dynamic texture and inviting matte surface, created with a specialized CMF treatment.

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: How durable is Galaxy Z TriFold?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold is built with strengthened hinge, glass and frame protection for improved durability. Strong, precision-built titanium hinge housing helps keep the two hinges protected and Armor FlexHinge is engineered to protect your device. Its wide hinge features a revolutionary spiral design that is slim without compromising durability. The cover screen is reinforced with durable Corning® Gorilla Glass® Ceramic 2 and Advanced Armor Aluminum increases the strength and hardness of the frame to help protect your device.8,9,10

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: How good is the camera on Galaxy Z TriFold?
chunks.x: The camera system on Galaxy Z TriFold is one of the most powerful on a Galaxy device, with a triple rear camera system, including a 200 MP Wide camera. ProVisual Engine utilizes our advanced processor to enhance image processing. Nightography delivers clear photos even in low-light settings. The 10 MP Front Camera, located on the main screen, features a 100-degree viewing angle for group selfies. The large main screen provides space for reviewing and editing photos, manually or with the help of Generative AI editing.1,23,25,26

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: What processor does Galaxy Z TriFold have?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold is powered by the advanced Snapdragon® 8 Elite, specially optimized for Galaxy devices. This processor is optimized to deliver faster CPU performance, advanced GPU graphics and an upgraded AI engine. It also enhances the versatile experience of this unique form factor, enabling intense multitasking, pro-level camera performance and on-device AI processing. The Snapdragon® 8 Elite also contributes to overall energy efficiency, optimized for both the large-capacity battery and the immersive main screen.10,28

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: What AI features does Galaxy Z TriFold have?
chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold includes AI tools designed to give you more convenient daily support. Gemini Live responds instantly to questions and can hold conversations for more complete answers. Share your screen or your camera to get information in real time. Writing Assist easily organizes and stores large summaries from websites. Transcript Assist transcribes voice recordings, summarizing them and providing keywords. Generative Edit helps remove unwanted objects, resize and reposition subjects and tweak images to your liking.13,15,16,25,26

chunks.x: Galaxy Z TriFold comes with One UI 8, optimized for our latest Galaxy Foldables. The redesigned interface makes everyday tasks more comfortable while boosting productivity and elevating multitasking on both the cover screen and the main screen. Customize your screen with wallpapers and interactive lock screen widgets for a personalized experience. Add interactive widgets to your lock screen to stay updated without needing to unlock your phone. You can also stay informed at a glance with features like Now Brief and Now Bar.34,35

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold

chunks.x: With Samsung DeX enabled, Galaxy Z TriFold is a premium Galaxy smartphone that delivers seamless, multi-workspace multitasking. You can create up to four workspaces and use Samsung DeX on the expansive main screen with a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse. Enjoy a multi-screen experience with a compatible monitor, moving apps between screens for a smooth and efficient workflow. Plus, connect to your monitor or smart TV wirelessly to share content on an even bigger screen and still get work done directly on your phone.30

chunks.t: Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold
chunks.h: What is the battery capacity on Galaxy Z TriFold and how long does it last?
chunks.x: The 5600 mAh battery on Galaxy Z Trifold keeps you powered throughout your day. The included 45 W Power Adapter enables super fast charging that gets you back to 100% in a short period of time. The battery is energy efficient thanks to the Snapdragon® 8 Elite processor and built-in software optimizations, giving you up to 17 hours of video playback time. Our mDNIe (Mobile Digital Natural Image engine) technology is built right in, efficiently enabling our bright displays to deliver a clear view without draining the battery.28,29,30,31

The box is made of a stunning matte black material, elevating the unboxing experience. It also contains a Carbon Shield case and Anti-Reflecting Film pre-installed on the cover screen to offer an additional layer of stylish protection to the already durable device. In the box you'll also find a 45W Power Adapter and data cable, granting immediate access to high-speed charging.32

It has ultra-level features: a 200 MP Wide camera, Snapdragon® 8 Elite processor and the 5600 mAh battery for up to 17 hours of video playback time. chunks.x: The new galaxy club program is only available with selected S25 models prior to June 20, 2025. The smart way to upgrade – and save – with new Galaxy Club benefits.1

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.x: Purchase your Galaxy S25 Series phone Choose Galaxy S25 Edge, Galaxy S25, Galaxy S25+, or Galaxy S25 Ultra. Select "New Galaxy Club" On the buy page, select "New Galaxy Club".

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: What do my monthly New Galaxy Club payments cover?
chunks.x: • A credit equal to 50% of your Galaxy S25 Series device MSRP that you could use towards your next phone purchase if you either pay in full or have paid off the balance for your Galaxy. • A credit equal to the remaining balance of your installments at time of your upgrade, if you chose Samsung Financing for your Galaxy S25 Series device purchase. • You'll need to continue making your monthly New Galaxy Club payments until your upgrade to be eligible for an upgrade benefit.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: How much will I pay when I upgrade to a new phone?
chunks.x: You will pay the current price of the new phone that you select, minus your upgrade benefit (value depends on the payment option that you used for your Galaxy S25 Series device purchase), minus any eligible promotions and discounts that are applicable at the time of your upgrade. You will have to turn-in your Galaxy S25 Series device when you upgrade.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: Can I turn in any phone when I upgrade?
chunks.x: No. In order to be eligible for an upgrade benefit you will have to turn in the Galaxy S25 Series device you purchased when you signed up for New Galaxy Club. When you upgrade, we will ask you to enter your Galaxy S25 Series device IMEI to confirm that you are turning in an eligible device.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: Do I need Samsung account in order to subscribe for the New Galaxy Club?
chunks.x: A Samsung account is not required to sign up for the New Galaxy Club with Pay in Full or Pay in 4 Installments. It is required if you want to use Samsung Financing.4 Signing up with a Samsung account will give you the benefit of tracking your New Galaxy Club subscription on your account page, and being able to cancel it without contacting Samsung Customer Service.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: When will I be charged my monthly New Galaxy Club fee?
chunks.x: Your first monthly fee will be charged after your device is shipped and its IMEI is registered in our systems. Corresponding fees will be charged every month after that.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: When will my New Galaxy Club subscription end?
chunks.x: Your subscription will end when you upgrade to a new phone and turn in your Galaxy S25 Series device, or if you cancel your New Galaxy Club subscription (on the My Account page or via Samsung Customer Service)

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: What happens if I don't want to upgrade after 12 months? Can I keep using my existing device?
chunks.x: You don’t have to upgrade at 12 months or after, but you will continue to be charged the full monthly New Galaxy Club fee until you upgrade or cancel your subscription. In addition, you will be charged monthly for Samsung Care+ starting from month 13 unless you cancel your Samsung Care+ or New Galaxy Club subscription.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: Can I cancel or get a refund for my Galaxy Club subscription?
chunks.x: You can cancel your New Galaxy Club subscription anytime on My Account page or via Samsung Customer Service. If you cancel, you will not be charged monthly anymore, but you will lose your Samsung Care+ subscription and your upgrade benefit. No refunds of the past monthly fees will be made in case of cancellation, but you will get a refund of your initial monthly fee in case you return your device within 14 days from your purchase date.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: When and how can I upgrade my phone to a new one?
chunks.x: You will be eligible for an upgrade benefit 12 months after your initial Galaxy S25 Series device purchase. You will receive an email from Samsung with a reminder on your upgrade and details when your eligibility draws near. The process will be similar to purchasing a new phone on samsung.com and trading in your old device.

chunks.t: New Galaxy Club | Early Upgrade Program
chunks.h: Can I subscribe to the New Galaxy Club in stores other than Samsung.com and will I be able to upgrade in other stores?
chunks.x: No. The New Galaxy Club is currently available exclusively on samsung.com. chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.x: The Frame TV is a unique TV that doubles as a piece of artwork when not in use. Unlike traditional flat-screen TVs, The Frame TV is designed to blend seamlessly into your home décor, transforming it into a beautiful, customizable art display. When in Art Mode, The Frame TV showcases a variety of digital artwork,1 photos, or personal images, allowing it to resemble a framed picture on the wall.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 2. Are Samsung Frame TVs good for gaming?
chunks.x: Yes, The Frame TVs are great for gaming. They offer low input lag, support for 4K resolution at up to 144Hz on select models, and HDMI 2.1 ports for next-gen console compatibility. Game Mode automatically optimizes settings for a smooth, responsive gaming experience.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 3. What are the benefits of The Frame TV?
chunks.x: The Frame TV and The Frame Pro TV blend advanced QLED and Neo QLED2 picture quality with a stylish picture-frame design. It transforms into artwork when not in use, features customizable bezels,3 and delivers vibrant colors, 4K resolution,4 and smart TV functionality, making it both a TV and a decor piece.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 4. Is it okay to leave the Frame TV on all the time?
chunks.x: Yes, you can leave The Frame TV on in Art Mode, which is designed to be energy-efficient and features a motion sensor to turn off the display when no one is in the room. However, for long-term energy savings and screen preservation, it's recommended to use the Auto-Off settings.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 5. How to connect The Frame TV to the internet?
chunks.x: You can connect The Frame TV to the internet either via Wi-Fi or an Ethernet cable. Go to Settings > General > Network > Open Network Settings, then select your preferred connection method and follow the on-screen instructions.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 6. What are the features of The Frame TV?
chunks.x: The Frame TV and The Frame Pro offer 4K QLED and Neo QLED2 displays with Quantum HDR,5 Art Mode, customizable bezels,3 Motion and Brightness Sensors, compatible with voice assistants (Bixby, Alexa, Google Assistant), Smart Hub, and access to popular streaming apps. It also supports Samsung’s One Connect Box 6 for clean cable management.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 8. How does Art Mode work on The Frame TV?
chunks.x: Art Mode lets The Frame TV display curated artworks or your own photos when the TV is off. A built-in motion sensor activates the screen when someone is nearby, and a brightness sensor adjusts the image based on ambient light, making the artwork look natural.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 9. What are the different sizes of The Frame TV available?
chunks.x: Samsung The Frame TV is available in various sizes. The classic The Frame (LS03FA) is available in 32”, 43", 50", 55", and 65", while The Frame Pro (LS03FW) is available in 65", 75", and 85".

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 10. Does The Frame TV come with free art?
chunks.x: Yes, Samsung's The Frame TV includes a rotating selection of free art through Art Store Streams. Art Store Streams gives you access to 30 pieces of art a month (360+ different pieces a year) to enhance your home décor. Samsung also offers a paid subscription to the Art Store for $4.99/month, giving you unlimited access to over 4,000 pieces of artwork from museums, artists, and organizations such as The Met, MoMA, Art| Basel, Art Institute of Chicago, Keith Haring, Basquiat, Salvador Dali and many more. The Art Store is refreshed on a weekly basis and includes recommendations and curations by Samsung’s team of art curators.

chunks.t: The Frame TVs: Stylish Design & Matte Display
chunks.h: 11. Does the Samsung Frame TV come with a wall mount?
chunks.x: Yes, Samsung's The Frame TV comes with a wall mount included in the box. Specifically, it includes the Slim-Fit Wall Mount, which allows the TV to hang nearly flush against the wall, enhancing its appearance as a piece of art. σYour rate for pay-over-time plans will be 0–36% APR. chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.h: What does 4K resolution mean on a TV?
chunks.x: 4K resolution is a high-definition display standard that offers incredibly sharp and detailed images. It gets its name from the approximately 4,000 horizontal pixels it has (3,840 pixels across and 2,160 pixels down, denoted as "3840x2160"). A 4K TV supports this resolution, making it perfect for watching movies, shows, and playing games with stunning clarity. With four times the pixels of a standard Full HD TV (1920x1080), 4K TVs deliver crisper details, smoother visuals, and a more immersive viewing experience.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.h: What is the difference between 4K TV and UHD TV?
chunks.x: 4K TV and UHD TV are the same, both offer 3840x2160 resolution.UHD stands for Ultra High Definition and is the consumer standard for televisions with a 3840 x 2160 pixel resolution.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.h: Is it worth buying an 4K TV?
chunks.x: If you want the best picture quality, a 4K TV is a great choice. It's especially worth it if you're upgrading from an HD or Full HD TV. Here's why, 4K has 4x more pixels than Full HD (FHD), making images much sharper. 4K has 9x more pixels than HD, offering an even more detailed and lifelike picture. For a better viewing experience, a 4K TV is definitely worth considering.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.x: 4K content is readily accessible in various forms. This includes 4K broadcasts, streaming services, and user-generated content captured with 4K cameras and smartphones. You can find such content on platforms like YouTube. Additionally, major streaming providers like Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+, they all support 4K.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.h: Is a 4K TV good for gaming?
chunks.x: A 4K resolution TV is ideal for gaming, as it provides a more immersive and ultra-fluid experience. Notably, the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC gaming, support 4K gaming, and Samsung Gaming TVs with HDMI 2.1 ensure a seamless 4K gaming experience.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.x: When you watch lower-quality FHD content on a 4K TV, upscaling is the technology that increases its resolution and optimizes it to fit the display panel of a 4K TV. It upgrades it for the 4K display. Upscaling automatically analyzes resolution to reduce noise, improve details and provide optimum contrast and color so that you can view the content in 4K-like quality.

chunks.t: 4K Smart TVs: High Definition & Smart Features
chunks.h: Can the human eye perceive 4K resolution?
chunks.x: Yes, the human eye can perceive 4K resolution. The difference between 4K resolution and low-resolution videos is quite noticeable when you are close to the screen, and can even be distinguishable from a distance depending on your eyesight.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail
chunks.x: 8K refers to screen resolution, specifically a pixel count of 7,680 horizontally and 4,320 vertically (denoted as "7680x4320"). 8K TVs support 8K resolution, which is the highest resolution TV available on the market.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail
chunks.h: What is the difference between 4K TV and 8K TV?
chunks.x: An 8K TV display has a pixel count of 7680x4320, which is four times more than 4K and sixteen times more than Full HD. A TV with 8K resolution delivers four times the sharpness and smoothness picture quality than the 4K TV. You'll enjoy a picture so detailed, it almost seems real.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail
chunks.h: Is it worth buying an 8K TV?
chunks.x: Upgrading to an 8K TV is worth it if you want to future-proof your home entertainment, as it's the highest level of TV technology available for home use. Plus, Samsung’s 8K AI upscaling technology transforms lower-quality content look incredibly near 8K quality, providing an exceptional viewing experience.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail
chunks.x: As a relatively new technology, there is less 8K content compared to other resolutions like 4K. However, platforms such as Samsung TV Plus and YouTube already support 8K content, and this support is expected to gradually expand in the future.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail
chunks.x: Samsung introduced its 8K TVs in 2019 with a specialized 8K AI Upscaling technology. Powered by the AI Quantum Processor 8K, it learns from millions of data points to enhance texture, reduce noise, sharpen edges, and optimize color, contrast, and detail for a premium viewing experience. The system gathers different image characteristics and stores them in a database, allowing it to recognize similar types of content later. This makes the upscaling process smarter and more effective over time.

chunks.t: 8K TVs: Ultra-High Resolution & Stunning Detail

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.x: A gaming TV is a television designed or optimized to enhance the gaming experience. It typically features low input lag, high refresh rates (like 120Hz), fast response times, and support for technologies like HDMI 2.1, Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), and 4K or higher resolution. These features reduce lag, screen tearing, and motion blur, delivering smoother, more immersive gameplay, especially with modern consoles like the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: What kind of TV is best for gaming?
chunks.x: The best TV for gaming is a 4K or 8K TV with 120Hz or higher for smooth play. If you want the best picture with true colors and deep blacks, go for an Neo QLED 4K TV. These features make for a top-notch gaming experience perfect for PS5, Xbox and PCs.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: Are Samsung TVs good for gaming?
chunks.x: Samsung offers excellent gaming TVs. Samsung 4K and 8K TVs boast high refresh rates up to 120Hz, with models like the Class OLED Gaming TV S95F reaching 144Hz (and some even higher) for smooth gameplay. Samsung TVs also offers anti-glare TVs for an enjoyable gaming experience.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: What is a refresh rate and how does it work?
chunks.x: Refresh rate (Hz) is how often a TV screen updates the image. Higher rates, like those found in 120Hz TVs, mean smoother motion, especially for fast-paced content like sports and gaming. For refresh rates above 120Hz, a PC connection is typically required. A higher refresh rate means less blur. Most Samsung TVs have a 60Hz refresh rate, which is standard for everyday viewing. However, many newer models, especially those geared towards gaming offer 120Hz or even higher refresh rates.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: What are motion rates vs refresh rates?
chunks.x: Refresh rate (Hz) measures how often a TV updates its image. Higher refresh rates mean smoother motion. Motion rate is not a direct measure of refresh rate, but a way to describe it. Both terms are related but mean different things.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.x: Yes, 4K TVs are great for gaming, offering sharp visuals, HDR, and larger screens. The Samsung Neo QLED 4K QN90F is a top choice for gaming, featuring Motion Xcelerator 144Hz for a smooth gaming experience.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate

chunks.x: Yes, OLED TVs are great for gaming monitors, delivering bright colors, deep blacks, and super-fast response times for a smooth play. With 120Hz+ and low delay, it’s perfect for PS5, Xbox Series X, and PCs.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate

chunks.x: Yes, The Frame TV performs well for casual and next-gen gaming alike. Select models support 4K at 120Hz with HDMI 2.1, making them compatible with PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X. With features like Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM), low input lag, and Game Mode, gamers can enjoy smooth, responsive gameplay without sacrificing design or picture quality.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: Are QLED TVs good for gaming?
chunks.x: Yes, QLED TVs are fantastic for gaming! They offer vibrant colors, high brightness and great contrast, making your games look stunning. With features like 120Hz, low input lag and HDR, QLED TVs provide a great gameplay experience for your PS5, Xbox and PC gaming.

chunks.t: Gaming TVs | Up to 240Hz Refresh Rate
chunks.h: Is QLED better than OLED for gaming?
chunks.x: Both QLED and OLED TVs have strengths for gaming, but the best choice depends on your priorities. QLED TVs offer higher brightness, no risk of burn-in, and are often better in bright rooms. OLED TVs, on the other hand, have perfect blacks and faster pixel response times, which can enhance visual clarity in dark scenes. For gamers worried about static HUD elements or long play sessions, QLED may be the safer option. But if you're after deep contrast and cinematic visuals, OLED has the edge. Both can support 4K at 120Hz, VRR, and low input lag, so either can be excellent for gaming.

chunks.h: Is Micro RGB better than OLED?
chunks.x: Micro RGB TVs and OLED TVs differ both in terms of technological structure and picture quality characteristics. Micro RGB TVs, based on RGB LED backlighting, use micro-sized RGB backlights to locally dim brightness and color, making them outstanding TVs in terms of both brightness and color performance. In fact, Samsung Micro RGB TVs meet 100% of the BT.2020 wide color gamut1 — the industry benchmark for color measurement — and are recognized for their precise color reproduction. chunks.t: OLED TVs: Ultra-Thin, Sharp 4K & Smart Features
chunks.x: An OLED TV is a type of display that uses self-lighting pixels to create its image. Unlike traditional TVs that rely on a backlight, OLED panels use organic compounds that emit light when electricity is applied — hence the name OLED, which stands for Organic Light-Emitting Diode. Each pixel in an OLED screen can be turned on and off, or have its brightness independently adjusted. This allows for incredibly precise control over contrast and color, resulting in deep, true blacks, vibrant visuals and ultra-responsive performance. Whether you're watching movies, gaming or streaming your favorite shows, OLED technology delivers a viewing experience that's hard to match.

chunks.t: OLED TVs: Ultra-Thin, Sharp 4K & Smart Features
chunks.x: Whether OLED TVs are worth it depends on your priorities and budget. Here are some factors to consider: • OLED TVs show true black and have amazing contrast, enhanced by Glare Free (S95F) anti-reflection tech and OLED HDR Pro/HDR+/HDR for balanced brightness and vivid visuals in any lighting. These features create a refined, immersive experience ideal for movies, dramas, and shadow-rich content. •︎ Stunning Brightness: Samsung OLED TVs achieve a high peak brightness for enhanced visibility in bright spaces and improved HDR performance, while self-emissive pixels ensure precise brightness control for true blacks and vibrant highlights. With OLED HDR Pro, the S95F delivers lifelike visuals with through its contrast and detail.

With Pantone Validated precision, they deliver lifelike visuals, ensuring creators’ intended colors are perfectly reproduced for an immersive experience. •︎ Fast response times for smooth gaming : Samsung OLED TVs feature fast response times, high refresh rates (up to 165Hz, available on select models), and gaming-specific technologies like Motion Xcelerator, ALLM, and AI Game Mode for smooth, lag-free gameplay. chunks.t: OLED TVs: Ultra-Thin, Sharp 4K & Smart Features
chunks.h: 3. What is the difference between OLED and QLED TVs?
chunks.x: The primary differences between OLED and QLED TVs lie in their display technologies, picture quality, and design. • OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode): Uses self-emissive pixels that produce their own light. Each pixel can turn off completely, enabling deep blacks and infinite contrast. •QLED (Quantum Dot Light Emitting Diode): Uses a backlight combined with quantum dot technology to enhance color and brightness. To learn more, check out our TV buying guide on What is OLED TV. It breaks down the differences between these types of TVs, and explains how these technologies work.

chunks.t: OLED TVs: Ultra-Thin, Sharp 4K & Smart Features
chunks.h: 5. Why Samsung OLED TVs Are an Outstanding Choice?
chunks.x: As we’ve seen, OLED TVs — in particular ones designed by Samsung — stand out as a worthwhile investment for anyone seeking exceptional visual quality, innovative features, and sleek design. With their vibrant picture performance, advanced gaming capabilities, and smart energy-saving options like AI Energy Mode, they cater to a wide range of lifestyles and preferences. Whether you're passionate about movies, gaming, or modern aesthetics, Samsung OLED TVs offer a premium experience that truly justifies their value.

chunks.h: 7. How to reduce glare on Samsung OLED TVs?
chunks.x: Glare occurs when light from windows, lamps, or other sources reflects off the TV screen, making it difficult to see the image clearly. While they offer stunning picture quality, OLED TVs can be more prone to glare due to their glossy screens. However, on Samsung OLED TVs, Glare Free, our proprietary anti-glare technology ensures that the image remains clear from distracting reflections.

chunks.t: OLED TVs: Ultra-Thin, Sharp 4K & Smart Features
chunks.h: 8. Is OLED worth it for console gaming?
chunks.x: Yes, a Samsung OLED TV is an excellent choice for console gaming, especially if you value premium picture quality and advanced gaming features. Here’s why Samsung OLED is worth considering for gaming. 1. Low Input Lag and Fast Response Time: Samsung OLED TVs are optimized for gaming with ultra-low input lag and fast response times, ensuring smooth and responsive gameplay. 2. Advanced Gaming Features: Samsung OLED TVs support HDMI 2.1, which enables features like 4K at 120 Hz (or higher) for ultra-smooth motion, Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) to eliminate screen tearing, Auto Low Latency Mode (ALLM) to automatically switch to gaming mode, and Nvidia G-Sync and FreeSync Premium Pro for enhanced compatibility with gaming consoles and PCs. 3.

chunks.x: Yes, OLED TVs are generally well-suited for watching sports due to several advantages: 1. Overall, if you prioritize picture quality, motion clarity and consistent performance from different angles, OLED TVs are a strong choice for watching sports.

chunks.h: What's the difference between OLED TVs and Micro RGB TVs?
chunks.x: Micro RGB TVs and OLED TVs differ in both technological structure and picture quality characteristics. Micro RGB TVs use micro-sized RGB LED backlighting to precisely control brightness and color through localized dimming. This enables strong brightness performance and highly accurate color reproduction. Samsung Micro RGB TVs meet 100% of the BT.2020 wide color gamut — an industry benchmark for color measurement — and are recognized for precise color expression. chunks.h: Which is better: OLED TVs or Mini LED TVs?
chunks.x: It's difficult to say which is better, as they're just different. The difference is that Mini LED TVs are known for their high brightness and ability to enhance HDR using small LED backlighting, while OLED TVs are known for creating deep blacks and strong contrast by lighting each pixel individually.

This makes the Samsung 2026 OLED S95H a standout choice for those seeking top-tier performance and features.

chunks.h: Are Samsung OLED TVs HDR (High Dynamic Range) TVs?
chunks.x: Yes, Samsung OLED TVs are HDR (High Dynamic Range) TVs. They support various HDR formats, including HDR10+ Advanced and HDR10+ Adaptive Gaming. These formats enhance picture quality by delivering greater brightness, deeper colors and improved contrast, making them ideal for watching sports and other content with dynamic visuals. For specific details about a particular model, please refer to its product detail page.

chunks.t: New 2026 OLED AI TVs
chunks.h: Does OLED have Deep blacks and infinite contrast?
chunks.x: Yes, One of the most notable qualities of OLED TVs is their ability to produce truly deep blacks. Since each pixel can turn off completely, there's no light bleed from a backlight — unlike on traditional LED TVs. This results in infinite contrast, where bright elements pop against pitch-black backgrounds, creating a more immersive and cinematic viewing experience, especially in dark rooms. Samsung OLED TVs take this a step further with Glare Free (S95H/S90H), an advanced anti-glare technology that ensures these deep blacks aren’t washed out by external reflections. This keeps dark scenes rich and precise, maintaining clarity without unwanted glare.

chunks.t: New 2026 OLED AI TVs
chunks.x: Another area where OLED TVs truly shine is in their ability to produce rich, accurate colors. This is because their self-emissive technology lets them fine-tune color output with remarkable precision. Colors stay vivid and well-defined — even in the darkest scenes — while pixel-level light control ensures sharp detail, especially with HDR content. On Samsung OLED TVs, the true blacks, infinite contrast, HDR support and uniform color distribution all work together to deliver colors that feel almost real. Additionally, with Pantone Validated, Samsung OLED TVs ensure colors are displayed with unmatched accuracy, matching the hues intended by creators. The result is a deeply immersive viewing experience that brings every frame to life.

chunks.h: Does OLED have good viewing angles?
chunks.x: Yes, OLED TVs have excellent viewing angles. This can be explained by the following reasons: - Self-Emissive Pixels: OLED TVs use organic light-emitting diodes that emit their own light. Since each pixel produces its own light independently, the image quality remains consistent regardless of the viewing angle. - Color Accuracy and Contrast: OLED TVs maintain accurate colors and deep blacks even at extreme angles. - Wide Viewing Angle Technology: Modern OLED TVs incorporate advanced panel designs that enhance viewing angles further, ensuring minimal distortion or color washout. There are several benefits of having wide viewing angles in Samsung OLED TVs: - Ideal for Multiplayer Gaming: Gamers can comfortably play with friends sitting at different angles without losing image quality.

chunks.t: New 2026 OLED AI TVs
chunks.x: Yes, OLED TVs are generally considered flicker-free thanks to their pixel-level lighting technology. This is because these displays use organic light-emitting diodes that emit light individually when electricity is applied. Each OLED pixel can turn on and off completely, eliminating the need for flickering to control brightness. Instead, on an OLED TV brightness is smoothly controlled through analog dimming, which varies voltage rather than rapidly cycling light. Benefits of having flicker-free OLED TVs include: - Reduced Eye Strain: Flicker-free displays are easier on the eyes, especially during prolonged viewing sessions. - Better Visual Comfort: Ideal for gamers, movie enthusiasts, or anyone who spends extended periods in front of the TV. - Consistent Picture Quality: No flickering…

chunks.t: QLED 4K TVs: Vivid Colors & Smart Features
chunks.h: What is a QLED TV? Is a QLED TV worth it?
chunks.x: A QLED TV uses tiny particles that glow when lit, called Quantum Dots, to deliver higher brightness and more accurate, vivid colors. Because each dot emits a precise hue, QLED displays maintain rich color no matter how bright the screen. It’s worth getting a QLED TV if you want a more immersive experience for movies, sports, or gaming. QLED screens create a vivid viewing experience that really draws you into the action.

chunks.t: QLED 4K TVs: Vivid Colors & Smart Features
chunks.h: What is the difference between QLED, OLED and Neo QLED TVs?
chunks.x: The major difference between Samsung QLED, OLED and Neo QLED TVs is the lighting technology. QLED TVs use nanoscale-sized particles called Quantum Dots illuminated by a traditional backlight. This technology provides vibrant colors and good brightness levels. Neo QLED TVs also use Quantum Dot technology like QLED TVs, but their backlight design is made up of mini-LEDs for more precise lighting control. This enhancement allows for better contrast and darker blacks compared to traditional QLED TVs. Samsung TVs with QLED technology (including QLED, Neo QLED, and Neo QLED 8K TVs) have been certified by TUV Rheinland as having Real Quantum Dot Display, meaning that the elements that make up the display meet International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) standards. A Real Quantum Dot Display…

chunks.t: QLED 4K TVs: Vivid Colors & Smart Features
chunks.h: Which is better, QLED TV or Crystal UHD TV?
chunks.x: QLED and Crystal UHD both deliver bright, colorful HDR images, and 100% color volume but QLED TVs go further by using Quantum Dots—tiny particles that emit highly precise colors. This gives QLED TVs enhanced brightness and superior color accuracy, which tends to make them more expensive. A crystal UHD TV is still great for everyday viewing, but if your budget allows and you want a more immersive experience for movies, sports, or gaming, a QLED TV is the better upgrade. *100% color volume measured in Movie Mode and the DCI-P3 color space, certified by VDE.

chunks.h: How do I choose a QLED TV?
chunks.x: When choosing one, start with screen size. Samsung offers QLED TVs from 32 inch Class to 85 inch Class. While a bigger screen size is better for immersion, also consider what can fit into your space. All Samsung QLED models offer 4K resolution for a sharp and detailed picture. They also support HDR, which enhances peak brightness and overall contrast. Cost depends on the exact model and specifications. Samsung QLED TVs come in a wide price range, giving you options to suit your budget.

chunks.t: QLED 4K TVs: Vivid Colors & Smart Features
chunks.h: What is Quantum dot TV technology?
chunks.x: Quantum dots are ultra-fine nanomaterials — tens of thousands of times smaller than a human hair — renowned for their ability to reproduce vivid, precise colors depending on the light wavelength. The way quantum dots are integrated into display panels has become a key indicator for evaluating technological advancement in the premium TV segment.

chunks.t: QLED 4K TVs: Vivid Colors & Smart Features
chunks.h: Are samsung QLED TVs performance tested?
chunks.x: Société Générale de Surveillance (SGS) has certified the quantum dot sheet used in 2025 Samsung TVs with QLED technology as being compliant with the EU’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive, and has been verified to contain no cadmium.* This certification shows that Samsung TVs with QLED technology are performance tested to contain no cadmium while delivering incredible picture quality. *SGS verifies that Samsung's Quantum Dot sheets used in its QLED TVs contain no cadmium. Cadmium is a restricted hazardous substance under the EU's RoHS directive that requires electronic products to contain less than 100 ppm of cadmium.

Smart Monitors: Turn on your Smart Monitor and navigate to the Samsung TV Plus app to start watching. Family Hub: On your Samsung Family Hub™ refrigerator, navigate to the Samsung TV Plus app to start watching. Web: Navigate to samsungtvplus.com and start watching from your web browser. chunks.h: How do I remove Samsung TV Plus?
chunks.x: Samsung TV Plus is an integrated feature of your TV and it can't be fully removed. However, if you remove all of the channels, Samsung TV Plus will not appear on your TV anymore unless a new channel is added. Periodically, new channels are added and you'll need to remove them if you don't want Samsung TV Plus. You can also remove the Samsung TV Plus app from your TV's Home screen. Simply highlight it, press Down, and then select Remove > Remove. Note: You can restore the TV Plus channels by performing a Smart Hub reset. But this will sign you out of all of your apps, so you have to make sure you have all of your login information and your TV's PIN code (default is 0000). Navigate to Settings, and then select Support. Select Self Diagnosis, and select Smart Hub Reset to perform the reset.

chunks.t: Samsung Smart Home & Smart TV with SmartThings
chunks.x: Samsung Smart Home is Samsung’s all-in-one smart living platform that connects devices like TVs, refrigerators, washing machines, lights, smart locks and more to make everyday life simpler and more convenient. You can manage and control these devices through the SmartThings app, a centralized hub that lets you connect, monitor and operate your smart home with ease. Most Samsung TVs come with SmartThings built in, so you can use your TV as a smart home manager without needing extra hardware. With features like Pet Care, Universal Gestures, Storage Share, 3D Map view and hands-free control using voice assistants, Samsung Smart Home brings added value — enabling TV control, smart device connectivity, home appliance management and family care.

chunks.t: Samsung Smart Home & Smart TV with SmartThings
chunks.h: How do I pair my Samsung TV with my phone?
chunks.x: There are two main ways to pair your Samsung TV with your phone, using Tap View or the SmartThings app. To use Tap View, follow the simple steps below. 1) Open the SmartThings app on your smartphone. 2) Tap Menu, then Settings. 3) Enable Tap View, Tap Sound, and tap OK to confirm. 4) Gently tap the back of your phone against the bezel of your TV, avoiding corners and the screen itself. 5) On your phone, tap Start Now. 6) When a prompt appears on your TV, select Allow to complete the pairing. To use the SmartThings app, follow the simple steps below. 1) Make sure your phone and TV are connected to the same Wi-Fi network. 2) Download the SmartThings app onto your phone. 3) Once installed, open the app and tap Add Device. 4) Choose your TV by scanning a QR code, detecting nearby devices, or…

chunks.h: What are the most important features to look for in a TV for watching sports?
chunks.x: Key features include AI upscaling to enhance sub-4K broadcast feeds, a native 120Hz+ refresh rate to help eliminate motion blur, high brightness and deep contrast, wide viewing angles, and glare-free technology for daytime viewing

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: Can I mute the commentary during a sports game without losing stadium crowd noise?
chunks.x: Yes. With the AI Sound Controller on 2026 Samsung TVs, the AI engine intelligently separates the announcer voice track from ambient stadium audio. You can use voice commands like “Mute the Commentary” to silence commentators and immerse yourself entirely in the roar of the crowd, or conversely, mute crowd noise to focus exclusively on the play-by-play analysis.1

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: What tv is good for watching sports?
chunks.x: The Samsung Micro RGB (R95H / R85H) is the ultimate next-generation choice for sports. Micro RGB uses thousands of individual microscopic red, green, and blue backlight LEDs (<100µm) to achieve 100% BT.2020 color coverage2, extreme peak brightness, and deep contrast to make daylight games vivid and jersey colors hyper-realistic.

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: Why is AI upscaling important for sports broadcasts?
chunks.x: Most live sports air in lower resolutions like 720p or 1080i SDR. Samsung's AI Upscaling analyzes incoming frames identifying edges and textures to reconstruct lost details and present the broadcast in near 4K clarity.

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: What refresh rate is recommended for sports?
chunks.x: A native 120Hz+ refresh rate is recommended to eliminate motion blur during fast plays. Samsung Neo QLED (QN80) can deliver 144Hz and Samsung OLED (S95/S90) and up to 165Hz with Motion Xcelerator for smooth, crisp action.

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: How does Glare-Free technology help during daytime games?
chunks.x: It helps eliminates window and light reflections without washing out color or contrast. Samsung Glare-Free OLED, NEO QLED, and The Frame use matte anti-reflection to enhance vibrant, rich colors without distracting reflections, even in bright or sunny rooms.

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: What is Samsung Multi View and how does it work for sports?
chunks.x: Multi View splits your display so you can watch two games simultaneously, or follow live fantasy stats side-by-side with the broadcast, or mirror your compatible mobile screen without missing live action.

chunks.t: TVs for Watching Sports - 4K UHD, QLED & OLED
chunks.h: How does Samsung AI Motion Enhancer reduce blur during live games?
chunks.x: Samsung AI Motion Enhancer Pro (powered by the NQ8/NQ4 AI processors) automatically detects ball and puck trajectories and rapid camera pans. It applies targeted frame smoothing directly to high-velocity action and fast-moving score tickers without creating artificial "soap opera effect" halos.

chunks.t: Mini LED vs. OLED : What's the difference?
chunks.x: TV Buying Guide In this article, we will examine the differences between Mini LED TVs and OLED technologies, which are both featured in Samsung's TV lineup. If you're looking for a TV with excellent brightness and HDR performance, Mini LED TVs — Samsung Neo QLED — are a great place to start. If you're searching for OLED TVs with the ability to truly deliver deep blacks and optimized contrast, Samsung OLED lineup features self-emitting pixels that highlight details in dark scenes. By the end of this guide, you'll have a better understanding of their distinct advantages, so you can find the right type of TV for your needs.

chunks.t: Mini LED vs. OLED : What's the difference?
chunks.x: Mini LED is a type of backlight technology that uses smaller LED lights compared to the ones used in standard LED — hence the name Mini LED. It delivers higher peak brightness, deeper black expression and better image control even in spaces with ambient light. In particular, Samsung Neo QLED premium lineup combines Quantum Matrix Technology with Quantum Mini LEDs. This allows more LEDs to be placed within a smaller area, enabling precise screen control for boosted brightness with accurate light management, so you can enjoy finer details in both the darkest and brightest scenes. In addition, the Quantum Dot Technology found in Neo QLED TVs offers superior color expression for a dynamic viewing experience.

chunks.t: Mini LED vs. OLED : What's the difference?
chunks.x: OLED (Organic Light Emitting Diode) is a display technology where each pixel is individually lit, allowing for deep black levels and well-balanced contrast. OLED excels at providing vibrant colors and rich blacks, making it an excellent choice for those who prioritize deep contrast and color accuracy. Used in Samsung OLED TVs, OLED is a premium display technology due to its ability to produce dark blacks and high contrast ratios.

chunks.t: Mini LED vs. OLED : What's the difference?
chunks.h: Mini LED vs. OLED: Picture Quality
chunks.x: Picture quality is a key factor that drastically affects your overall viewing experience in terms of how realistic and immersive the content appears, down to the finest details. Additionally, it determines the TV's ability to showcase accurate color, contrast and motion. Compared to traditional LED, Mini LED display optimizes picture quality in Samsung Neo QLED TVs by enhancing brightness with rich color rendition, delivering better HDR quality. Meanwhile, OLED displays achieves outstanding image quality through its ability to produce excellent deep black levels and balanced whites, creating a striking combination of depth and clarity on Samsung OLED TVs.

chunks.t: Mini LED vs. OLED : What's the difference?
chunks.h: Mini LED vs. OLED: Brightness & Color
chunks.x: Brightness is essential for visibility and overall viewing experience, especially in terms of color expression. Mini LED displays enhances brightness by illuminating specific zones as needed, creating a natural and balanced viewing experience in both bright and dark environments. Samsung Neo QLEDs feature QLED technology and Quantum Dot-based color expression, delivering a richer range of color across all brightness levels for bright, realistic hues. chunks.x: A QLED TV uses Quantum Dot layers that set it apart from standard LED TVs. So, what is a Quantum Dot? Quantum Dots are ultra-fine semiconductor materials of nanoscale size. These tiny dots produce different colors of light depending on the particle size — larger particles emit red while smaller particles emit blue. They radiate precise colored light because the particle sizes adjust at quantum-level velocities, resulting in accurate and efficient light emissions. The result? A tremendous boost in image quality, brightness, contrasts, and color.

chunks.h: How to choose the best TV for watching sports
chunks.x: To find the best TV for watching sports, prioritize features like AI upscaling, which enhances lower-resolution broadcasts (such as 720p or 1080i) for sharper, clearer picture quality. Additionally, consider larger screen sizes (75” or more) to create an immersive in-game feel, along with brightness, wide viewing angles, and glare-free technology to maintain picture quality from every angle. Choosing the best TV for sports involves evaluating several key factors to ensure an optimal viewing experience. Below are the most important aspects to consider.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.h: Key Features for a sports TV
chunks.x: The best TVs for sports keep up with fast, unpredictable action, delivering an immersive experience. High brightness ensures visibility in bright rooms, while deep contrast enhances the drama of night games. Wide viewing angles allow everyone in the room to enjoy the action. For rich blacks and incredible detail, OLED TVs excel. If your space receives a lot of natural light, Glare-Free OLED is an excellent choice for maintaining clarity in bright environments. For smooth sports performance at a lower price point, Crystal UHD offers strong value. QLED TVs also provide vibrant colors and wide viewing angles, making them a solid option for watching sports. When comparing models, focus on features that work together to deliver a clearer, more lifelike game-day experience.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Resolution and HDR are critical features for sports TVs, even with AI upscaling. AI enhances the existing picture, but higher-resolution TVs with better HDR processing offer superior color depth, contrast, and brightness. While AI upscaling improves lower-resolution and SDR (Standard Dynamic Range) broadcasts, they cannot match the picture quality of a 4K HDR TV.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: A native refresh rate of 120Hz (or higher) reduces motion blur during fast-paced action, making visuals cleaner and more natural. This feature is essential for tracking deep passes, hat tricks, or breakaway drives.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Prioritize motion blur handling to ensure smooth visuals during games. Technologies like AI upscaling and high refresh rates (120Hz or higher) help you stay locked on every play. Samsung's AI Upscaling2 analyzes each frame, identifying edges, textures, and numbers to rebuild lost details in lower-resolution broadcasts. This enhances clarity on jerseys, field markings, and fast-moving graphics, making televised games appear in 4K.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: To determine the ideal TV size for sports, multiply your viewing distance (in inches) by 1.2 for a 40-degree field of view—optimal for 4K TVs. For example, sitting 8.5 feet (102 inches) away suggests an 85-inch screen for an immersive experience. This ensures clear visibility of player movements and stats.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Glare-Free technology is essential for sports TVs, virtually eliminating reflections in bright rooms while maintaining sharp colors, contrast, and details. Samsung's Glare-Free technology excels in this area, ensuring consistent picture quality even during daytime games or in well-lit environments.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Samsung Multi View is a standout feature for sports enthusiasts. It allows you to watch two games simultaneously, follow live stats alongside a game, or mirror your phone screen—all on one screen. This is ideal for fans who want to track multiple matchups without switching devices or missing key moments.

chunks.t: Best TV for Watching Sports: TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: High-quality sound is crucial for an immersive sports-watching experience. Look for TVs with advanced audio technologies like Dolby Atmos and Object Tracking Sound to create a three-dimensional soundscape that enhances spatial awareness during games. Pairing a Samsung TV with a soundbar unlocks Q-Symphony, delivering synchronized audio from both devices. play Indicator 1

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: What is TV contrast, and why does it matter?
chunks.x: Contrast refers to the difference between the bright whites and dark blacks on a TV. Premium TVs like OLED and Micro RGB feature high contrast ratios, which enhances detail and realism. TVs with high contrast deliver more vivid colors and highlights, and more visual depth. TVs with lower contrast ratios show images that tend to appear flat and dull, making it harder for the human eye to perceive the differences in various parts of the screen. Why contrast should be a top buying priority

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: Superior contrast makes every scene more lifelike
chunks.x: Contrast determines how deeply you see shadows, highlights, and details on screen. That adds up not only to richer blacks and brighter whites, but enhanced depth and texture across all the content you’re watching. Contrast determines whether you see detail or lose it Contrast measures how a TV displays detail across bright and dark areas of the screen. Strong contrast preserves shadow depth, highlight clarity, and overall realism, while weaker contrast can make images appear flat or washed out.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: AI helps bring contrast to the next level
chunks.x: Artificial intelligence can further boost contrast by analyzing what you watch in real-time, adjusting brightness, shadow detail and highlight intensity scene by scene.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: Contrast matters in both bright and dark rooms
chunks.x: In darker spaces, strong contrast improves black depth and shadow detail. In brighter rooms, where glare, reflections or ambient light may be a consideration, contrast helps images maintain clarity and separation.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.x: Contrast ratio measures the difference between the brightest white and darkest black a TV can display. For example, a contrast ratio of 5,000:1 means the TV’s brightest white is 5,000 times brighter than its darkest black. OLED TVs have a near-infinite contrast ratio. play Indicator 1 These features are important for contrast No matter which model you’re considering, all Samsung TVs feature powerful technologies that help create contrast. Here’s a primer to help you understand them.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: How does Local Dimming affect contrast?
chunks.x: Local Dimming technology in models like Samsung’s Neo QLED TVs improves contrast by allowing different areas of the screen’s backlight to brighten or darken independently based on the content being shown. Micro RGB has thousands of even smaller zones, reducing light blooming around bright objects.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: Is Full Array Local Dimming important for contrast?
chunks.x: Full Array Local Dimming technology is well suited for viewers who want a more cinematic and immersive picture experience. TVs like Samsung’s Micro RGB combine a full array backlight grid with independently controlled local dimming zones to improve contrast across the screen.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: How does high dynamic range (HDR) help contrast?
chunks.x: HDR expands the range between the brights and darkest parts of an image. Many Samsung TVs support advanced HDR formats such as HDR10+, which dynamically optimizes brightness and contrast on a scene-by-scene basis. This helps ensure that bright areas, like sunlight or reflections, appear more vivid without washing out details, while darker scenes retain shadow detail instead of appearing flat or crushed.

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.h: How does AI help improve contrast?
chunks.x: AI processors like Samsung's NQ4 AI Gen3 can help improve contrast by analyzing scenes in real-time, boosting highlights and rendering finer details1 in both bright whites and deep shadow. Features such Samsung Vision AI’s Adaptive Picture Mode and Real Depth Enhancer analyze content in real time to improve contrast scene-by-scene. What TVs have good contrast?

chunks.t: TV Contrast Guide: OLED & High Contrast TVs
chunks.x: OLED TVs create contrast through self-emissive pixels that can turn off completely, producing true blacks and near-infinite contrast. This allows dark areas of the screen to remain black while bright elements stay distinct. chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.x: Explore All Buying Guides What is HDR? And when it comes to HDR, HDR10, and HDR10+, what do these different acronyms mean? Let's delve into the details behind these terms and explore the transformative benefits of HDR meaning and technology.

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.h: What does HDR mean on a TV?
chunks.x: HDR (High Dynamic Range) improves the contrast between very dark and very light colors on a TV screen. HDR technology means you can see everything happening on screen the way it was intended, with true-to-life colors, shadows and detail – giving the ultimate TV viewing experience. In daily life, your eye is able to perceive more detail, color and a wider range of light than what typical televisions can offer, but with HDR technology the eye is served a much more accurate representation of reality. Now you can see what’s lurking in the shadows of a horror movie or witness the true beauty of a sun-filled scene in pin-sharp clarity.

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.x: HDR10 is the original and most common variation of HDR that you might come across. If manufacturers want to associate this term with a TV, it means that the TV must reach a certain standard based on color subsampling, bit depth and other factors. To put it simply, the TV has to produce a certain standard of picture quality and this is measured against a variety of criteria.*

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.x: Samsung pioneered HDR10+ technology, setting a new standard for HDR. HDR10+ is widely used across Samsung TV ranges and serves up a glorious viewing experience. While HDR10 sends advanced picture data to the TV when the content loads, HDR10+ improves on this technology by sending updated instructions scene-by-scene, resulting in more detailed highlights and a better overall picture.

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.h: How is HDR different than resolution? And is HDR better than 4K?
chunks.x: Full HD and 4K are types of resolutions, whereas HDR is a feature that enhances picture by improving highlights. HDR technology improves the colors and contrast on the TV screen which, depending on the scene, can provide a more impactful TV viewing experience. Conversely, 4K delivers a sharper, more detailed image which looks more true-to-life than Full HD. The great news is that 4K and 8K TVs are often HDR compatible, so you can enjoy the color and contrast of HDR with the quantity of UHD, providing a breathtaking viewing experience. Additionally, 2023 Samsung TVs support Auto HDR Remastering, upgrading standard content into dazzling HDR. Want to learn more about 4K TVs and 4K resolution? Visit our helpful article on 4K TVs.

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.h: What is the difference between HDR vs non-HDR TVs?
chunks.x: HDR displays can show a larger color depth and more dynamic range than non-HDR displays. So essentially, HDR lets you see details in the dark shadows and highlights in one scene. With standard dynamic range (SDR), either one is usually blown out or crushed, so you cannot see the detail in them.

chunks.t: What are HDR TVs and What Does HDR Mean?
chunks.x: Due to HDR’s ability to create high contrast between light and dark areas on screen, HDR technology is perfect for gaming.* Particularly for gamers who enjoy playing first-person shooter, exploration or high intensity games on a console or PC. Discover Samsung’s range of Gaming TVs or learn more about how to pick the best gaming TV for you.

chunks.h: What is the difference between Micro RGB and RGB Mini LED?
chunks.x: Both Micro RGB and RGB Mini LED technologies utilize LED lights. The key difference is Micro RGB features LEDs that measure less than 100 microns, where RGB Mini LED lights typically range between 100–400 microns. These tiny lights or diodes enhance LED TVs by enabling them to use thousands of light sources behind the screen for precise local dimming, exceptional contrast, and real black levels3.

chunks.t: What is Micro RGB TV? | 4K TV Technology Guide
chunks.x: Micro RGB and OLED TVs offer exceptional picture quality, but have different advantages. Contrast & Black Levels: OLED TVs provide nearly infinite contrast and true black levels due to self-emissive pixels that turn off completely. Micro RGB TVs have excellent contrast and black levels, while OLED TVs have cinematic contrast. OLED TVs brightness paired with its incredible contrast ratio creates amazing picture quality. Brightness: Both Micro RGB and OLED TVs excel in brightness. Micro RGB uses synthetic components that allows them to reach peak brightness, while OLED TVs achieve high brightness by using self-emissive Quantum Dot technology, making them both a great choice for movies, TV shows, and gaming. Additionally, select models5 of OLED and Micro RGB TVs feature glare-free…

chunks.t: What is Micro RGB TV? | 4K TV Technology Guide
chunks.x: ally, select models5 of OLED and Micro RGB TVs feature glare-free technology, ensuring an optimal viewing experience even in varying light conditions. Color: Micro RGB TVs offer a wide color gamut that covers 100% of the BT.2020 color area, by using dedicated red, green, and blue LEDs without filters. OLED TVs deliver Pantone® validated color with exceptional vibrancy and accuracy, leveraging their superior contrast capabilities to cover 100% of the DCI-P3 color area. Is Micro RGB the same as Micro LED? No, they are different technologies. Micro RGB is an advanced LED backlight technology that uses tiny red, green, and blue LEDs. Micro LED is a self-emissive technology that does not use any backlights. Micro RGB vs Micro LED: Structure: Micro RGB uses a densely packed array of micro-sized…

chunks.t: What is Micro RGB TV? | 4K TV Technology Guide
chunks.x: . Micro RGB vs Micro LED: Structure: Micro RGB uses a densely packed array of micro-sized red, green, and blue LEDs that work together as a backlight. Conversely, Micro LED is a self-emissive light display where each individual pixel is a tiny LED that emits its own light. Micro RGB vs Micro LED: Contrast & Blacks: Micro LED uses a self-emissive, microscopic LED light that can turn off completely, providing deep blacks and nearly infinite contrast ratios. Micro RGB uses thousands of micro-sized, red, green, and blue LEDs as a backlight, enabling precise control over bright and dark colors. This results in real black levels3 and exceptional contrast. chunks.h: Part workplace, part classroom, all home
chunks.x: No longer tied to spaces like the office or the classroom, the way we work and learn is changing. We're spending more time at home and looking for ways to use our TV as a computer monitor. Samsung Smart TV gives us the flexibility to thrive remotely and the ability to easily do it all. Remote Access makes working feel like no work at all Work without missing a beat with Remote Access and PC on TV.1 Even if your computer is back at the office, TV on PC automatically recognizes it, so you can access your files, update documents and collaborate with colleagues on Office 365 — all from your TV.2

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Explore All Buying Guides Are you interested in buying a 4K TV and wondering whether it's the right choice for you? Maybe you'd like to learn more about what 4K means and how it impacts the way you watch TV. Check out our 4K TV buying guide for more information about 4K technology and what it means for your viewing experience.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: With an ever-increasing amount of streaming shows and movies being produced in 4K, you'll want to take advantage of higher resolution shows and movies with an ultra high definition (UHD) TV that can display 4K content in all its glory. But what does 4K mean, exactly? The term 4K refers to the resolution of your TV—in the same way that your might think about High Definition TV. The difference between an HD TV and a 4K TV is that the latter provides 4 times more pixels, creating a crystal clear picture for optimal TV viewing. And now that 4K has arrived, there are plenty of types of 4K TVs to choose from. If you’re in the market for a new TV, it’s definitely worth checking out a few different types of 4K TVs from Samsung, like the Samsung Neo QLED 4K TV, The Frame or Crystal UHD 4K TV.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: Put simply, a 4K TV is a TV with 4K resolution. The “K” in 4K stands for Kilo (1000), meaning a TV that has achieved a resolution of almost 4,000 pixels wide (3840 x 2160), which is four times the total pixel count of Full HD displays (1920 x 1080). HD resolution is often referred to as 1080p, while 4K is called 2160p. When we refer to TV resolution, we’re talking about the density of the pixels on your display. Individual pixels collect together to make up the image you see on the screen, so the higher the pixel count, the higher the resolution. If there are fewer pixels and they’re dispersed further apart from your screen, you could see a fuzzier picture. If there are more pixels and they’re displayed close together, you’ll get a much clearer picture.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: 4K upscaling is the technology that increases lower-quality resolution to 4K by converting and optimizing it to fit the display panel of a 4K TV. In other words, it doesn't just stretch the image—it upgrades it for the 4K display. Upscaling automatically analyzes resolution to reduce noise, improve details and provide optimum contrast and color so that you can view this content in 4K-like quality. So if you were to come across content that isn’t developed with 4K in mind, your viewing experience won't be impacted.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: The difference between 4K and HD is simple—4K TVs have four times more pixels than traditional Full HD (1920 x 1080) TVs. Even on TV screens of the same size, the 4K TV picture quality ends up being more vivid and detailed thanks to the greater pixel density—which makes them especially great TVs for gaming. This difference is particularly obvious on big screen TVs. For example, if you compare the picture quality of an HD TV with a 65” 4K UHD TV, you'll notice the pixels are smaller than a lower-resolution TV of the same size. That means you'll enjoy a more immersive experience and a crisper picture.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: UHD stands for Ultra High Definition and generally refers to any TV with a 4K or greater resolution. When choosing between a 4K or a UHD TV, you needn’t worry—they are the same and just as good as each other.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.x: If you are researching different types of 4K TVs you will likely come across Crystal UHD. This refers to a lineup of Samsung televisions that display 4K resolution. There are various expressions to talk about 4K including 4K TV, Ultra UD, Ultra High Definition TV and 4K UHD TV. They all are essentially the same thing. UHD is an industry standard for TVs that display 4K. Samsung Crystal UHD TVs have advanced processors to display high-quality 4K with enhanced color. Today, most manufacturers and distributors now use the term 4K TV or 4K UHD TV. Recently, another type of UHD TV has begun to show up on the market: the 8K TV.

chunks.t: What are 4K TVs? | 4K TV Buying Guide
chunks.h: What’s the difference between 4K TV and 8K TV?
chunks.x: Exactly in the same way that 4K differs from HD TV, 8K has four times as many pixels as 4K—and even more impressively, up to 16 times as many pixels compared to a 1080p TV. Ultimately, more pixels result in a sharper, clearer image and 8K offers up an impressive 160 pixels per inch (PPI), delivering a truly smooth and crisp image. Learn more about what the difference is between 4K TV and 8K TV.
